Your practice. Your information.

This page describes the current Beter preview and how to ask about your data.

Private preview · Policy review required. This draft needs the operator’s approval before public launch.

What Beter handles

  • Account email, an account identifier, verification status, and sign-in sessions.
  • Virtual portfolios, practice bets, quotes, balances, and ledger history. Beter does not take deposits or accept real-money wagers.
  • The email, topic, message, and reference number you provide when you contact support.
  • Technical request and security information used to operate and protect the service. Shared abuse limits store hashed quota keys instead of raw emails or source addresses.

Where information goes

AWS provides account sign-in, application hosting, encrypted PostgreSQL storage, operational logs, and backups. Support requests pass through AWS notification services to the operator’s configured email mailbox. That mailbox and its email provider also process the request; it is separate from the app’s AWS storage.

We use account and practice information to provide the app, maintain ledger consistency, investigate faults, and protect access. We use support details to review the request and verify ownership when needed. Do not send passwords or verification codes.

In your browser

Connected account sessions use secure, HttpOnly cookies. Anonymous practice and sample portfolio views can save practice data in this browser. Clearing browser site data removes that local copy; it does not delete a Beter account or its connected history. Self-hosted fonts are included with the app.

Retention and your choices

Active records, security logs, backup copies, support notifications, and virtual ledger records have different operational purposes. This preview does not promise a fixed deletion deadline. The operator reviews requests, explains applicable retention, and removes or deidentifies information where appropriate. Ledger integrity records may be retained in deidentified form, and backup copies follow their configured retention or cleanup process.

You can request access, correction, or a review of your information using the support form. Account changes and deletion require manual ownership verification; submitting a request alone does not establish ownership.
